eyebrow: AI Engineering Leadership & Architecture · Chapter Three
titlePlain: What Changes When You're the Senior
subtitle: Lesson 11 · Technical Leadership & Influence

eyebrow: A different job, not more of the same job
code:
Mid-level:        being right, faster and more reliably
                   than most people in the room.

Senior-most:      being right is necessary --
                   but no longer sufficient.
caption: If the room doesn't understand why, you solved today's problem and created tomorrow's.

code:
Instead of:   "Here's the answer."

Try:          "Here's the question we should
               actually be asking."
              "What would make us confident
               one way or the other?"
caption: A room that reasons its way to a conclusion owns it. A room that was just told never does.

code:
The senior engineer who answers
every question, every meeting,
because they genuinely can --

quietly teaches the team that
raising a hand beats thinking it
through, until the team's judgment
stops developing.
caption: Then the senior engineer leaves, and the team can't make decisions it used to make easily.

eyebrow: When the direct answer is actually right
code:
Knowledge gap:     "What does this specific
                    API actually return?"
                    -> Usually fine to just answer.

Judgment call:      "Should we build or buy
                    this component?"
                    -> Usually better facilitated.
caption: The skill is noticing which situation you're actually in.

subtitle: The meeting a design document is written for.
